heading: Live dashboard

overview.participantsNote: People who have rated at least one study

leaderboard.heading: Leaderboard
leaderboard.introScore: Who predicts the group best? For each study, participants guess the average rating it will get. A guess scores 100 points, minus {penalty} for every point it is away from the scoring target (rounded to a whole number and never below 0).
leaderboard.introTarget: The scoring target is the expert rating counted as if {weight} participants had given it, averaged with the ratings other participants had given the study by then, in every room.
leaderboard.introRules: Accuracy is a person's average score per rated study, rounded to a whole percentage. Only people who have rated at least {count} studies are ranked; people who have rated fewer are not listed. When two people have the same accuracy, the one who rated more studies is placed higher, and if that is also the same, they share a place. Select a username to see that person's results.
leaderboard.dayNote: Showing people whose latest rating was saved in the past 24 hours.
leaderboard.emptyAll: No one is ranked yet. People appear here once they have rated {count} studies.
leaderboard.emptyDay: No one ranked has rated a study in the past 24 hours.

unranked.one: {count} more person has rated fewer than {min} studies and is not ranked yet.
unranked.other: {count} more people have rated fewer than {min} studies and are not ranked yet.

leaderboard.truncated: Only the top {count} places are listed.

criteria.heading: Which criteria matter most
criteria.intro: After rating, each participant shares out {budget} tokens among the {count} criteria, giving more to those they think matter most when judging a study. The bars show the average share of tokens each criterion received and the dark lines their 95% confidence intervals (t distribution). Interval limits below 0% or above 100% are shown as 0% and 100%.

count.one: Based on {count} participant who shared out all their tokens.
count.other: Based on {count} participants who shared out all their tokens.

criteria.empty: No one has shared out their tokens yet.
criteria.ciMissing: An interval needs at least two participants.

chart.heading: Ratings by study
chart.introBars: Each bar is the average quality rating that participants gave a study, on the scale from 1 to 7. Only participants' ratings count: the expert's rating is not part of the bar.
chart.introIntervals: The dark line on each bar is the 95% confidence interval for that average, worked out with the t distribution. It is long when people disagree or when few have rated the study, and missing when fewer than two have. Where an interval runs past 1 or 7, it stops at the edge of the chart without an end cap; the tooltip and the table give its full limits.
chart.introExpert: The white diamond is the expert's rating. The bar colour shows the expert's quality band, which the height of the diamond also shows.
chart.introTarget: Predictions in the game are scored against a different value: the expert rating counted as if {weight} participants had given it, averaged with the participants' ratings. While few people have rated a study, that target stays close to the expert rating rather than the participant average shown here.
chart.introSelect: Select a bar, or a study in the table below, to read the study and the expert's feedback.
chart.canvasLabel: Bar chart of the participants' mean rating for each study, with 95% confidence intervals and the expert rating. The table below gives the same figures.
chart.tooltipMeanSingle: Participant mean: {mean} (n = 1, too few for an interval)
chart.summary: {rated} of {total} studies have participant ratings. For {close} of them, the participant mean is within one point of the expert rating.
chart.summaryNone: No study has participant ratings yet.
chart.failed: The chart could not be loaded. The table below has the same figures.

table.heading: Statistics by study
table.intro: Every figure comes from participant ratings only; the expert's rating has its own column. 'Ratings' is the number of participants who rated the study, 'SD' (standard deviation) shows how much their ratings vary and '95% CI' is the confidence interval for the mean. 'Mean prediction' is the average of participants' guesses of how others would rate the study. A dash means there are too few ratings: the SD and the interval need at least two.
table.sortHint: Select a column heading to sort the table. The 95% CI column sorts by its lower limit.
table.regionLabel: Statistics by study (scrolls sideways on small screens)
